title: Australia's constitution lists trade and commerce with other countries and among the states as a federal legislative power
summary: Australia's constitution lists trade and commerce with other countries and among the states as a federal legislative power.
body: Section 51 grants Parliament power, subject to the constitution, to make laws with respect to trade and commerce with other countries and among the states, and it continues with a list that includes taxation. The source says: "th with respect to: trade and commerce with other countries, and among the States; taxation; but so as not to discriminate between States or parts of States; bounties on the production or export of goods, but so that such bounties shall be uniform throughout the Commonwealth; borrowing money on the public credit of the Commonwealth; Telecommunications postal, telegraphic, telephonic, and other like services; the naval" The grant is a listed head of power. It is not a statement that the states have no remaining powers.
